title: Open images of field groupoid morphisms are closed
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $V=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $(V,R_1,s_1,t_1,e_1,i_1,c_1)$ and $(V,R_2,s_2,t_2,e_2,i_2,c_2)$ be absolute groupoid schemes [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Let $a:R_1\to R_2$ be a morphism which, together with $\mathrm{id}_V$, commutes with all groupoid operations. If the image $a(|R_1|)$ is open in the underlying topological space $|R_2|$, then $a(|R_1|)$ is closed in $|R_2|$. No finite-type, separatedness, quasi-compactness or perfectness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Put $H=\operatorname{im}|a|$ and choose $r\in\overline H$. Apply the point-lifting node to $R_2,r$, obtaining $K/k$ and $r^{\prime}\in R_2^{\prime}$ above $r$ with both residue-field maps invertible. Restrict both groupoids along $\operatorname{Spec}K\to V$ using the restriction node. The original morphism induces $a^{\prime}$ on triples by $(u,z,v)\mapsto(u,a(z),v)$; the displayed operations commute with it since those of $a$ do. By the fibre-product universal property its square with the middle projections is Cartesian. The projection-image formula gives $H^{\prime}:=\operatorname{im}|a^{\prime}|=p_2^{-1}(H)$, so $H^{\prime}$ is open. For every open neighbourhood $N$ of $r^{\prime}$, openness of $p_2$ makes $p_2(N)$ a neighbourhood of $r$ meeting $H$. Thus $N$ meets $H^{\prime}$, and $r^{\prime}\in\overline{H^{\prime}}$. It suffices to prove $r^{\prime}\in H^{\prime}$, which projects to $r\in H$.

Work with the restricted groupoids, omitting primes and writing their field as $k$. The identity point belongs to $H$ because $a e_1=e_2$. The translation node gives an automorphism $L_r$ with $L_r e_2=u$, where $u:V\to R_2$ has image $r$ and $s_2u=\mathrm{id}_V$. Therefore $L_r(H)$ is an open neighbourhood of $r$. Since $r\in\overline H$, choose $x\in H$ with $y=L_r(x)\in H$.

source.place: Tag 04Q6, second proof paragraph, through the nonempty intersection.

proof.text: The inverse laws give $i_2(H)=H$, since $i_2a=ai_1$ and $i_1^2=\mathrm{id}$. Set $P_j=R_j\times_{s_j,V,t_j}R_j$. By the induced-map image formula, every point of $P_2$ whose projections lie in $H$ lifts to a point of $P_1$ under $a\times_Va$ (the object map is $\mathrm{id}_V$). The morphism $j:R_2\to P_2$ with components $(L_r,i_2)$ exists because $s_2L_r=s_2=t_2i_2$. At the chosen $x$, both projections of $j(x)$ belong to $H$: they are $y$ and $i_2(x)$. Lift $j(x)$ to $z\in P_1$. The groupoid laws give, on every test scheme, $c_2(c_2(u t_2(w),w),i_2(w))=u t_2(w)$, by associativity and the inverse and identity laws. Thus $c_2j=u t_2$ as scheme morphisms. The point $c_2(j(x))$ is consequently $r$, since $V$ has one point and $u$ has image $r$. Compatibility with composition yields $r=c_2((a\times_Va)(z))=a(c_1(z))\in H$. Step 1 now proves every point of $\overline H$ belongs to $H$, so $H$ is closed.

source.place: Tag 04Q6, final three sentences, with scheme-point lifting and cancellation written explicitly.
